title: Terminal output in an .astro template breaks the build two different ways
summary: An .astro file's whole template is compiled to a JS template literal AND its markup braces are Astro expressions, so pasting real command or source output into the markup fails the build twice over. (1) `${...}` is interpolated - a line like `redis.set(`sess:${token}`...)` fails with 'token is not defined'. (2) `{...}` is parsed as an expression - `JSON.stringify({ uid: user.id })` fails with 'Expected } but found await'. HTML-entity escaping does NOT fix either one: `${token}` is decoded back to `${token}` before the literal is emitted. The fix that works is to put the output in a frontmatter array of plain strings and map over it - frontmatter strings are immune to both - which is what `readOut` in demo/index.astro does. A THIRD, separate trap in the same territory: Astro also collapses template newlines, so a transcript written as one text block under white-space:pre renders as a single wrapped line; each line needs its own element. All three were found by building and rendering, never by reading the markup.
incidentAliases: astro build fails on terminal output

steps.role: carries the fix - terminal output as a frontmatter string array, mapped into one div per line
also renders terminal blocks; same rules apply to any output pasted here

invariants: Never paste raw command or source output straight into an .astro template. If it contains `$` followed by a brace, or any `{`, the build fails.
HTML entities do not escape either construct - the entity is decoded before the template literal is emitted.
One element per output line, because Astro collapses template newlines and white-space:pre alone will not save it.
The output box needs its own overflow-x:auto so long lines scroll inside the box instead of overflowing the page on mobile.
